mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: Exposure-limit discriminator for a symptomatic lever; not a treatment proposal and not an efficacy claim.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

drug_assertions.note: Label sections 5.3, 5.4 and 8.4 and the boxed warning were read in full from the JSON; the cited study itself was not read, so the 22 and 4 percent figures are the label's statement of it. The label states that the specific pattern was not observed in older children and adults. Vigabatrin only. Section 5.3 also records postmarketing MRI changes in children 6 years and younger treated for refractory complex partial seizures. 22 percent is the prevalence in the vigabatrin-treated infants of that study (non-WWOX, infantile spasms) and 4 percent the comparator on other therapies; arm sizes are not in the label. Batch ORCH-SCIBATCH-DR-20261105 (B1): three independent centres put the rate among imaged children between 22.1 and 44.7 percent (one at partial full-text depth, the others at abstract level); the one cohort reporting its exposed denominator gives about 26 percent per exposed child; and unexposed comparators exist (7 of 52 in one cohort; 4 percent of naive infants in the controlled study). These are frequencies in selected cohorts, not attributable risk in WWOX.

p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: Exposure-limit question for the one drug class with human WWOX-DEE partial-benefit reports (GABA-aminotransferase inactivators): is the vigabatrin brain-MRI abnormality (intramyelinic edema) liability different in a Wwox-deficient juvenile brain with a myelin deficit (mouse) or white-matter loss (patients; hypomyelination itself unresolved), and does it extend to the sibling inactivators; spasm control is carried only for the sibling.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for any sibling in a Wwox system. For vigabatrin in WWOX: single-patient efficacy and null reports on card EB-VGB-01, and two children with the MRI finding (abstract level). No rodent study of vigabatrin or a sibling in a Wwox-deficient animal was found.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: The vigabatrin liability is exposure-window dependent in rats and dogs (start age, dosing window, dose level) and reversible on stopping in those species; the human infant data are retrospective. A constitutive Wwox-null mouse dies within weeks, so whether a Wwox-deficient animal survives the vulnerable window is not established here.

cellular_context.target_expression: UNKNOWN: ABAT expression and GABA-aminotransferase activity in Wwox-deficient brain, and in oligodendrocyte lineage cells, are not measured in any record read.
cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: Myelinating tracts of the developing brain; the neuron-specific Wwox deletion has about 3.3 times fewer myelinated callosal axons at P17.
cellular_context.limits: The myelin deficit and the vigabatrin liability are both about myelin, but no experiment joins them; the word vacuole is shared with the Wwox rat-mutant hippocampal vacuoles and proves nothing about a shared mechanism.

p4_card.identity: A class card for two GABA-aminotransferase (ABAT) inactivators: vigabatrin (CHEMBL89598, approved, ChEMBL curated mechanism INHIBITOR) and CPP-115 (ChEMBL parent CHEMBL146927, salt CHEMBL4297273, clinical candidate by ChEMBL, max phase 1, no curated mechanism row). Guide to Pharmacology (ligands.csv, release 2026.3.1) lists ligand 8284 CPP-115 with ChEMBL id CHEMBL146927 and the same InChIKey as the catalogue record, and an ABAT interaction typed Inhibitor; the catalogue keeps its DGIdb record of CPP-115 (CAT:DGIDB:0a2199127751) as a separate family because the DGIdb concept id is an IUPHAR ligand id and not a ChEMBL id (identity proof by identifier, not by name; see the cycle README). OV329 (a further sibling) is not in the catalogue and is cited only through PubMed abstracts.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: Not an indication and not a treatment proposal. It asks whether the exposure limit of the only class with human WWOX-DEE partial-benefit reports is different in this disease. Nothing measured with one compound is transferred to another: vigabatrin rows stay on vigabatrin, CPP-115 rows on CPP-115, and no sibling row is read as evidence about brain MRI because none measures it.
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: PARZIALMENTE_TROVATO: the susceptibility question is posed in the last sentence of the Choi 2026 abstract and the label states the myelin liability; the repository holds the VABAM signal (CLAIM 001) and, separately, a rat-mutant vacuole hypothesis (intramyelinic oedema, analysis notes lde_myelin_vacuole_bridge and new_discovery_node). A search of those notes and of superior_node_search finds no mention of vigabatrin or VABAM, so the two have not been put side by side before. Not 'never done': only PubMed, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and the catalogue were searched.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: EB-VGB-01 (efficacy reports against the MRI finding, status CONTROVERSA, no next measurement defined); working-model position of caution for vigabatrin; CLAIM 001, CLAIM 031; needs NEED-INHIBITORY-HYPOFUNCTION (direction uncertain) and NEED-MYELINATION.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE, Track A (variant-independent). Safety side of a symptomatic lever.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. A genotype difference in the rodent lesion would move the working-model sentence from 'documented in WWOX-DEE' to 'enriched or not enriched in WWOX-DEE'; no difference would leave the two reported children without a WWOX-specific reading (they would remain a case-selected report with no denominator). Neither outcome says anything about benefit.
p4_card.mechanism: Vigabatrin irreversibly inactivates GABA-aminotransferase and raises brain GABA. Its brain lesions are described with different morphology by species: in immature rats the abstract of one electron-microscopy study reports splits of the myelin sheath along the intra-period line, with vacuoles more prominent at later stages of myelin development and lesion location following the myelination timetable; in juvenile dogs the abstract and the label describe gray-matter neuropil vacuolation not shown to be intramyelinic; the label calls juvenile-rat vacuolar changes distinct from adult intramyelinic edema, says the relation between the animal findings and the infant MRI changes is unknown, and records intramyelinic edema in infants from post-mortem examination (the one autopsy case read here has a pre-existing white-matter lesion; a second autopsy abstract describes white-matter spongiosis). Vacuolation reversed on stopping in rat and dog. Whether the human MRI finding follows from GABA-aminotransferase inactivation as such (a class effect) or from vigabatrin specifically is not established in any source read; the sibling designs address the retinal metabolite hypothesis, not any brain lesion. Direction for a Wwox-deficient brain is open in both ways: a prolonged immature-myelin window could raise the liability; fewer myelinated axons could lower the substrate (the repository's own counter-argument on the vacuole bridge). Batch ORCH-SCIBATCH-DR-20261105 (B1; every item NOT WWOX EVIDENCE, abstract level unless a row of this card says partial full-text) leaves the GABA direction unsigned. DATO: GABA alone reproduced a mild myelinated-fibre toxicity in culture without producing intramyelinic oedema; cerebrospinal GABA was higher in two cases, both preterm with post-haemorrhagic hydrocephalus; two genetic conditions that raise GABA show reduced myelination (the SSADH-deficiency cohort read at partial full-text depth, the GABA-transaminase-deficiency report at abstract level), with gamma-hydroxybutyrate correlating almost as strongly in one; endogenous GABA acting on GABA-A receptors reduces oligodendrocyte lineage number and myelination, while GABA-B engagement accelerates precursor differentiation and promotes remyelination; and vigabatrin depletes taurine and inhibits taurine transport, with taurine deficiency reported as the cause of its retinal lesion. INFERENZA: the liability may be a property of raised GABA in a myelinating brain, but the axis has opposite signs by receptor class and a molecule-specific rival exists, so neither a class reading nor a molecule reading is established. IPOTESI and its discriminator: a matched-engagement comparison of two inactivators in one juvenile model with one white-matter readout, plus receptor-subtype arms. No source read measures it.

for: The question changes a decision: the working model carried VABAM in WWOX-DEE as a safety signal that distinguishes WWOX (corrected in BATCH_20261019_025 to: documented in two case-selected children, no denominator, enrichment not supported) and the card EB-VGB-01 has no next measurement; a genotype-by-exposure test in a juvenile rodent window is a concrete, falsifiable next act.

The vigabatrin lesion is reproducible in rat and dog (in the rat it begins at the myelin sheath; in the dog it is described as gray-matter neuropil vacuolation) and its timing follows the exposure window, so a Wwox-deficient model with a myelin deficit gives a prediction in each direction rather than a vague worry.
The Choi 2026 authors themselves ask whether delayed myelination confers susceptibility, and the baseline MRI of both children showed white matter volume loss.
A pre-existing myelin abnormality was named in the pathology case report of 2009 as a reason for concern.
against: Two children selected for having the finding, with no denominator, cannot be shown to exceed (or fall below) the label's figures: 22 percent MRI changes in vigabatrin-treated non-WWOX infants with infantile spasms against 4 percent on other therapies (retrospective, N=205, arm sizes not stated). The denominator of vigabatrin-exposed WWOX children is not in any source read, so 'enriched in WWOX' is not supported and 'documented in WWOX' is all that holds.
Several WWOX vigabatrin reports on EB-VGB-01 describe no follow-up MRI, so an absence of VABAM in them is an unmeasured cell and not a negative.

Rival explanations for the WWOX findings: concurrent hormonal therapy (associated with symptomatic cases in one non-WWOX cohort, not with the MRI finding in another, both partial reads), disease severity, the underlying white matter disease, and observer bias.

The rodent and dog lesions were found at doses inside the human range, but vacuoles in neonatal and juvenile rats are described as distinct from the adult intramyelinic edema; the species bridge to a human infant is partial.

No Wwox-deficient animal has been given vigabatrin in any source found, and the constitutive null may not survive the vulnerable window; the neuron-specific deletion's survival into that window is not established here.

The sibling compounds: CPP-115 has one human infantile-spasms case (open label, concurrent vigabatrin, ketogenic diet, no repeat MRI described), a phase 1 healthy-volunteer record (cocaine dependence) and rat data; OV329 has rodent anticonvulsant data only. The retinal advantage rests on an ERG in rats. None measures brain myelin, so 'gentler on the retina' must not be read as 'gentler on myelin'. In the rat spasm model the highest CPP-115 level was lethal.
Access: no registered trial of CPP-115 in infantile spasms or of OV329 was found on ClinicalTrials.gov; supply route unknown.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: Species (rat, dog, human infant), exposure window, compound, and disease (non-WWOX infantile spasms, cerebral palsy, tuberous sclerosis) all differ from a WWOX-deficient brain.

p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN. Vigabatrin is a marketed prescription drug (catalogue: openFDA NDC listing). CPP-115 is, in the catalogue, a clinical candidate with no approval statement; ClinicalTrials.gov (API v2, 2026-10-28) shows one completed phase 1 study (cocaine dependence) and no infantile-spasms study; the single patient report used an investigational protocol. No contact was made. For the experiment named below only a rodent study is needed, whose supply is not assessed.
p4_card.time_to_benefit: UNKNOWN, separately from access. This card pursues no benefit endpoint; the earliest decision it can change is a safety framing, after one rodent exposure-window experiment.
p4_card.pharmacology: Vigabatrin: irreversible GABA-aminotransferase inactivation; boxed warning of permanent vision loss, with no dose or exposure known to be free of risk and vision assessment recommended at baseline, every 3 months and after stopping; MRI abnormalities in infants (label section 5.3); the label calls routine MRI surveillance unnecessary in adults and is silent here on surveillance in infants; the label describes a REMS program that certifies prescribers, patients and pharmacies (access is controlled, not absent). The label does not mention glucose or hypoglycaemia. CPP-115: ChEMBL max phase 1 without a mechanism row; Guide to Pharmacology lists an ABAT interaction typed Inhibitor with a lower constant than vigabatrin. Re-examined in IT5 (pharmacology_it5_20261029/abat_gabaat_h02.tsv): that constant is the KI of a time-dependent inactivation, not an equilibrium inhibition constant and not an IC50; the Guide values are printed in a review the Guide cites and are labelled human, whereas the primary papers deposited in ChEMBL used pig brain enzyme (the same vigabatrin figure also sits in a ChEMBL record with a guinea-pig assay organism under a human target mapping, a parallel route and not shown to be the Guide's source); no measurement on a human enzyme was found for any of the three compounds (a search result, not a universal negative: the human-tagged ChEMBL rows are unknown-origin or patent text); the direction (CPP-115 a more efficient inactivator than vigabatrin, OV329 a lower KI than CPP-115 in one same-assay pig comparison) is reproduced, the magnitude is not: two incompatible derivations of the 187-fold efficiency ratio are in print (the 2012 article attributes it to the 2003-type values, which give about 52-fold; only the review's own set reproduces 187), the same-assay KI values of 2020 differ by about five-fold, and vigabatrin's own KI differs about eleven-fold between the 2003 and 2020 pig-enzyme papers, so KI values from different papers are not like-for-like; an enzyme-level advantage says nothing about brain myelin, and the 2012 article states that no histology of CPP-115 for intramyelinic oedema existed; healthy-volunteer target engagement by spectroscopy (abstract); ERG data in rats (abstract). Doses and concentrations are deliberately not reproduced.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Not assessed beyond the sources: vigabatrin is labelled for infants 1 month to 2 years as monotherapy in infantile spasms and the vision and MRI warnings are pediatric-relevant. A mixed-therapy note: the CPP-115 case overlapped with vigabatrin and the ketogenic diet, so interactions cannot be separated.

p4_card.predictions: Registered before any such experiment: if the Wwox-deficient juvenile brain is more susceptible, vigabatrin at an exposure window and level that leaves control littermates without lesion produces vacuolation by electron microscopy (splits at the intra-period line) or a further fall in myelin markers in the Wwox-deficient animals, with the lesion at a location that follows the timetable of myelination in that genotype. If susceptibility is lower or equal, no genotype difference appears at matched exposure, and the two reported children carry no WWOX-specific reading from this experiment. If the Wwox-deficient animals do not survive the window, the experiment is not informative. A negative at unconfirmed brain exposure refutes nothing.
p4_card.next_measurement: Rodent: a Wwox-deficient juvenile model that survives the exposure window (the neuron-specific deletion is the candidate; survival is to be checked first) against control littermates, vigabatrin against vehicle at an exposure window and level taken from the published rat studies, with confirmed brain exposure, blinded electron microscopy for intramyelinic splits, myelin markers and g-ratio, and a pre-planned genotype-by-treatment interaction test; a sibling arm only if a supply exists. Human, no contact made: a structured case count of every WWOX-DEE child given vigabatrin (denominator), with follow-up MRI done or not, age at start, duration, hormonal co-therapy and outcome, in the natural-history or registry route already noted in the clinical census.
p4_card.value_added: Adds the missing next measurement for the vigabatrin thread; recasts the WWOX VABAM signal as numerator-only (no denominator), set beside the label's 22 versus 4 percent in non-WWOX infants; blocks the inference that a retina-sparing sibling is brain-myelin-sparing; joins, for the first time in the repository, the vigabatrin myelin lesion and the Wwox myelin deficit and vacuole questions; and records that CPP-115 sits in the catalogue as two unlinked families (identity proof by Guide to Pharmacology).

Earlier census 2026-10-20 found no registered WOREE interventional study. A missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not a WOREE-specific search for this card.

leads_needs_note: Handoff rule: coverage pairs for this card are listed only for these needs. The card does not claim symptomatic seizure control (NEED-SEIZURE-CONTROL-SYMPTOMATIC) and does not offer ABAT inactivation as a lever; it asks an exposure-limit question.
